lessons.title: shared-expert multistream stream-sync refactor breaks Ascend ms-ON path — 'forward is overridden' is a false no-op
lessons.symptom: runs 31811865858/31889914421/31952700363/32101793062 (8/14-8/18): test_multistream_overlap_shared_expert[32-vllm-ascend/DeepSeek-V2-Lite-W8A8] failed 9+ consecutive e2e rounds with AssertionError: Test1: — ms-ON vs ms-OFF first-token deterministic flip (' located!!!' vs ' that!!!') at temperature=0, 15+ retries bit-identical.
lessons.root_cause: upstream 47ececb58e ([Perf][ROCm] Dual-stream decode with hipgraphs #48223) restructured the shared-expert overlap machinery: moe_runner.py replaced _maybe_sync_shared_experts_stream + SharedExpertsOrder.MULTI_STREAM_OVERLAPPED with self._shared_experts.maybe_forward_async() before dispatch and wait() after routed experts, and shared_experts.py added torch.cuda.Event() pairs + _should_enable_stream_overlap_heuristic. vllm-ascend's ms-ON path (AscendSharedExperts.forward in vllm_ascend/ops/fused_moe/shared_experts.py, unchanged since 8/1) runs gate_up/down on a dedicated stream synchronized by events around the routed-experts dispatch — precisely the lifecycle this commit restructured, so the sync surface changed and a cross-stream race read stale buffers. The adapter dismissed it as no-op ('AscendMoERunner._forward_impl fully overrides the upstream flow') because the refactor touched wrapped-module control flow (streams/events/ordering), not any overridden method. Upstream reverted 47ececb58e via #52024 (landed 8/13); syncing past the revert restores the test.
fix_guidance: When an e2e failure is a first-token deterministic divergence between an OPTIONAL feature path (ms-ON) and the baseline, suspect async/stream/event sync changes in the WRAPPED upstream module, not the overridden forward.

Diff-check the wrapped module's control flow in the upstream patch: stream sync, Event creation/recording/wait, call ORDER of maybe_forward_async/wait vs dispatch/combine, heuristic gating (_should_enable_stream_overlap_heuristic).
'forward is overridden' is not evidence of no-op: AscendSharedExperts wraps the upstream SharedExperts module whose async lifecycle executes on the wrapper's behalf.
Reference: upstream vllm/model_executor/layers/fused_moe/moe_runner.py + shared_experts.py at the target commit; vllm-ascend vllm_ascend/ops/fused_moe/shared_experts.py (AscendSharedExperts.forward).
If the break is a known upstream refactor already reverted (e.g. #52024), the correct adaptation is to advance the verified commit past the revert, not to patch the Ascend side.

lessons.title: upstream deleted the is_internal_router gate branch — NPU MoE receives hidden_states as router_logits (bias assert + EP lora splits)
lessons.symptom: PR #14376 CI (run 31989107166, main lane only; v0.27.1 control passed): (1) test_mtp_spec_decoding[full_decode_only-False-32-wemaster/deepseek_mtp_main_random_bf16] failed during profile_run with 'RuntimeError: The bias first dim should be same as x second dim' (TORCH_CHECK(bias_size[0]==expert_num) in csrc/moe/moe_gating_top_k/moe_gating_top_k_torch_adpt.h:47, via AscendFusedTopKRouter._compute_routing -> DeviceOperator.moe_gating_top_k); (2) test_qwen3moe_lora_multi_id_ep failed with 'RuntimeError: Split sizes doesn't match total dim 0 size' in dist.all_to_all_single (vllm_ascend/ops/fused_moe/token_dispatcher.py:540 EP path), then HCCL AlltoAllV deadlock (507001) -> EngineDeadError.
lessons.root_cause: upstream fd04edef3e ([Refactor] Delete dead code in models #51838, 8/11, never reverted) deleted the is_internal_router branch in DeepseekV2MoE.forward (model no longer computes gate itself — always passes router_logits=hidden_states, relying on the runner to apply the gate) and removed the is_internal_router properties from FusedMoEWithLoRA/MoERunner plus ep_rank/physical_expert_start/physical_expert_end from Qwen3MoeSparseMoeBlock. Dead-code cleanup on CUDA (runner applies gate internally) but LIVE on NPU: AscendMoERunner._forward_impl (vllm_ascend/ops/fused_moe/fused_moe.py) only recomputes logits when is_internal_router (gate.weight_fp32 present, DSv4-only), so bf16 models (MTP: n_routed_experts=72, topk_method=noaux_tc, scoring_func=sigmoid) feed hidden_states [T,2560] into moe_gating_top_k expecting [T,72] -> bias assert. Same commit's qwen3_moe.py/lora fused_moe rewrites changed the contract the Ascend EP+lora assembly (AscendFusedMoEWithLoRA + prepare_lora_indices -1 padding) absorbs -> out-of-range topk_ids in mixed-lora EP batches -> histc(splits) sum != numel -> all_to_all split mismatch. UNRESOLVED on vllm-ascend side (both tests blocked in main2main per-step e2e).
fix_guidance: NPU-side fix must make the runner apply the gate for ALL MoE models (not only is_internal_router), matching upstream's new 'runner applies gate' contract; guard against double-application for DSv4 (is_internal_router still true there) and MiniMax-M2's model-side gate patch.

Check e_score_correction_bias flow: upstream deepseek_v2.py builds nn.Parameter(config.n_routed_experts) 1D; the op contract (1D, len==router_logits.shape[1]) is correct — the bug is WHAT is passed as router_logits, not the bias shape.

For EP+lora: the old all_to_all_single token_dispatcher is frozen legacy (upstream moved to all2all_manager); verify topk_ids stay in [0, num_experts) in mixed-lora batches (-1 padding from prepare_lora_indices interacts with the dispatch) or re-architect onto upstream's new EP path.
Unrelated symptom pairing: 'too many values to unpack (expected 20)' at npu_fx_compiler is a separate torch_npu compile bug (L20260810-era, qwen3_5_0_8b) — do not conflate.

lessons.title: guarded call sites but unguarded imports crash fixed branches (v0.27.1) — import new symbols under vllm_version_is
lessons.symptom: PR #14517 CI (run 32179691708, 8/18): the v0.27.1 control lane failed at scale — cpu-0 with 'ImportError: cannot import name BatchReqState from vllm.v1.worker.gpu.model_runner', and every a2-1 part with 'TypeError: init_workspace_manager() takes from 1 to 2 positional arguments but 3 were given' (test_qwen3_reranker_lora, test_llama32_lora, test_ilama_lora, test_lora_with_spec_decode, pooling/classification...). The main lane was unaffected.
lessons.root_cause: The adaptation (vllm_ascend/worker/v2/model_runner.py) added BatchReqState to a module-level import and added a third positional argument to init_workspace_manager (upstream _num_workspace_lanes) — both for the vLLM-main signature. The call-site version guard existed and the adapter asserted it was correct, but the module-level import was unguarded (crashes at import on v0.27.1) and init_workspace_manager got no version branch (crashes at call on v0.27.1). A guarded call site does not protect an unguarded import.
fix_guidance: After adding a version guard, grep the edited file for module-level imports of any symbol that does not exist in v0.27.1 (upstream-added names) — move them inside the vllm_version_is branch or import lazily at the use site.
Function signature changes (new positional args, e.g. init_workspace_manager(device, ubatches, lanes)) need a version branch: old signature under vllm_version_is("0.27.1"), new under else.

Verify with the dual-version CPU-UT when the touched module is importable there; otherwise rely on the PR CI v0.27.1 lane and do not claim the guard is correct until the import line itself is inside a guard.
Reference: vllm_ascend/worker/v2/model_runner.py (prepare_inputs batch_req_state) and vllm_ascend/worker/worker.py (init_workspace_manager call site).
